findings.reason: min over a group of a refreshing table that holds both 0.0 and -0.0: the two servers keep different zeros. Java keeps one entry for both in its sorted multiset and shows the zero that entry was made with, even after the row with that zero is gone (engine/table/src/main/java/io/deephaven/engine/table/impl/by/ssmminmax/SsmChunkedMinMaxOperator.java, chosen in AggregationProcessor#makeMinOrMaxOperator for a table that is not add-only). PARITY.md A2 would allow it and is proposed, not in force (Q4), so it stays a finding. Recorded seeds: --ops agg_by 337, 351, 785.

The same as agg-by-min-zero-sign, through agg_all_by: which of 0.0 and -0.0 the minimum of a refreshing group shows (SsmChunkedMinMaxOperator; PARITY.md A2 is proposed, not in force). Seeds: --family aggregations 252, 632, 813 as generated when the finding was written down.

agg_all_by with first of an append-only table: Java copies the AppendOnly attribute to the result (engine/table/src/main/java/io/deephaven/engine/table/impl/BaseTable.java, APPEND_ONLY_TABLE_ATTRIBUTE is copied for CopyAttributeOperation.FirstBy, applied in QueryTable#aggAllBy for AggSpecFirst). Oxhaven's result does not carry it.

An absolute sort of a table that is already in the order asked for (or is empty) and carries AppendOnly: Java's result has lost the attribute, because the handler sorts a view with an added column and drops the column again (server/src/main/java/io/deephaven/server/table/ops/SortTableGrpcImpl.java, updateView of the absolute columns, sort, dropColumns), and that chain does not pass the attribute on. Oxhaven answers with the attributes of the source, as both servers do for a plain sort that changes nothing.

The same as sort-absolute-keeps-append-only for a source that carries both AddOnly and AppendOnly: Java's absolute sort loses both (SortTableGrpcImpl.java: updateView, sort, dropColumns), Oxhaven keeps both.

aj on refreshing tables: after a step, what Java kept up to date differs from what Java answers when the same join is made again from the same rows (runlog/journal.md, 'As-of join: Java's ticking result differs from its own static result': a NaN left stamp joined to a newly added NaN right row under the rule >, and chains of aj whose left table depends on the right one keeping a match that is gone). Oxhaven gives the answer Java gives from scratch and agrees with itself. Counted only when Java's two answers do differ for the scenario at hand. Recorded seeds: --ops aj 39, 257, 1319, 1774, 2619, 2, 465, 540, 675, 1371, 1427, 1735, 2110, 2669, 2873.
The same as aj-reference-history, for a table with more differing cells than the comparison lists one by one: the 'truncated' note that ends such a list (recorded seed: --ops aj 675).

emstd_time over values that include an infinity, on a refreshing table: what Java keeps up to date differs from what Java answers when the same update_by is applied again to the same rows (Infinity against NaN), so there is no single reference answer. Oxhaven agrees with itself (selfcheck) and with Java's answer from scratch. Counted only when Java's two answers do differ for the scenario at hand.
